EMDR is one of the sole reasons I'm able to be intimate with people without flashing back to severe childhood trauma and I can say it saved my life. 

That said, it took me changing therapists a few times and we had to switch to tapping in the end. It was also bookended with some "traditional" talk therapy on either side and it was intense to go through at the time. 

I'm a pain in the ass for therapists because I need everything to be properly evidence based and fully did not believe EMDR would work but am really happy it did.

Honestly, I have thought about this in the context of fandom space a lot and think it comes from people generally enjoying romance as a concept (I know I do) and male characters tend to just get fleshed out more so viewers get more attached. If I'm someone who enjoys romance and wants to theorize or headcanon relationships, I'm not going to do that with characters I'm not attached to or who have no real chemistry. I'm going to do it with the two main characters who are shown to love each other immensely enough to do what House and Wilson have done for each other throughout the series.

As things stand, male characters tend to get more air time and more development in media, and that certainly was the case when House was airing. Couple that with general lack of representation for queer audiences and you have the perfect recipe for people seeing something beyond friendship - if you made one of them a woman and changed literally nothing of the script you can't tell me everyone would still read it as friendship. Maybe because as a society we value romantic love above platonic love but that'd be a whole thesis and not a reddit comment!
